SLC-500 ADVANCED PROGRAMMING SOFTWARE
The purpose of this lesson is to introduce you to the functions and operation of the Allen Bradley APS (Advanced Programming Software) software.

The APS software is used to create, manage, and implement ladder logic program files for the SLC 500 PLC in the Nida PLC Trainer. After you have learned how to effectively use the APS software, creating ladder logic programs will be fast and effective.

In this lesson, you will learn through an interactive simulation of the APS software. It is important to note that we will be covering just the basics of the APS software. For more advanced operation, please refer to the APS software manual...ffective.

The display shown below is the "Main Menu" and will appear any time you enter the APS program. Observe the listed information.....
There are three types of files that we will be talking about: processor, program, and data files.
Processor files are the files you will send to the PLC via a transfer cable. A processor file contains both program and data files.
Processor files contain user instructions, data, and configurations. Processor files can be transferred from a computer to a PLC or vice versa.
Some PLC systems use modems to communicate with distant PLC's.
Program files contain three program types: the system program, main ladder program, and the subroutine ladder program. These three programs are required for every processor file.

You can have anywhere from 3 to 255 program files. File 0 is reserved for the system program; files 1 and 2 are for the main ladder program; and files 3 through 255 are for the subroutine ladder programs...
The system program contains I/O configuration, the processor type and name, and other system oriented information.
The main ladder program contains user program instructions which tell the processor how to operate.
Subroutine ladder programs are short segments of program code that can be retrieved (called) from the parent program for the purpose of performing repetitive operations.
Data files contain information used by the main and subroutine ladder programs. As with the program files, certain data files have pre-defined types.
The pre-defined types are the first 9 files: file 0 - output data,
1 - input data, 2 - status data, 3 - bit data, 4 - timer data, 5 - counter data, 6 - control data, 7 - integer data, 8 is reserved for the system, and 9 - 255 are user definable.
The user defined data files will contain information needed by the program, but they must be of a type listed in the first eight.
Which of the following files belongs in a program file?
A data file is contained within a processor file, not a program file.

CHANGING THE PLC PROCESSOR MODE
Before you learn how to transfer programs to the PLC, it is important to understand the PLC's modes of operation. The PLC must be in the proper mode for proper operation.
DISCUSSION
There are many different processor modes for the SLC-500 PLC. We will discuss two of these modes: program and run.
In the program mode, processor files can be transferred to/from the PLC from the computer. In this mode, no program execution is being performed.
It is necessary to change to this mode before attempting to transfer a processor file to the PLC.
In run mode, ladder programs are executed and their output can be monitored. It is important to note that the ladder program files cannot be modified while in run mode.
In run mode, however, you can modify the processor data files. This is very helpful when fine tuning a ladder program. You can also transfer a processor file from the PLC to the computer.
